cross_sector_overview: Across every sector, governance and integrity scrutiny is rising (algorithmic tools such as the NDIS and aged care assessment tools and robodebt-style AI risk, coroner and watchdog findings, fraud and probity concerns), and it is colliding with tightening budgets and workforce and capacity strain. That points to sustained demand for PEPI work in assurance, system redesign, AI and automated-decision governance, costing and viability, and evaluation, particularly where Commonwealth and state funding settings are being renegotiated.

pepi_wide.brief: The week's dominant signal is implementation strain and accountability scrutiny across PEPI's core portfolios. In aged care, the Act's first anniversary coincides with roughly 200,000 people waiting for support, a damning Ombudsman finding that the IAT is an unreasonable 'technological black box', a government-commissioned tool review (criticised as marking its own homework) and a watchdog test of whether reforms have worked. That points to assessment redesign, automated-decision governance and provider-viability work, with IHACPA funding built on three-year-old costs. Fiscal pressure is the common thread: Treasury is reportedly resisting a $38b NDIS savings plan, allegations of a $170bn budget black hole are circulating, and Victoria is weighing infrastructure cuts, which signals Budget-driven efficiency, costing and prioritisation demand. Child protection coroner and regulator findings, education's national exams and AI/screen reset, and Housing Australia governance questions add review, evaluation, assurance and probity pipeline. Robodebt-style AI risk in government and integrity scrutiny of major transport projects reinforce demand for AI governance, delivery assurance and independent oversight advisory.

synthesis.brief: Health affordability and access dominate: specialist out-of-pocket fees (Grattan/Conversation) and the contested private health insurance rebate changes (including pensioner impacts) point to likely Medicare/PHI reform design work, while GP bulk-billing incentives are lifting coverage to almost two-thirds of Australians. Labor's $1.5b emergency wait-time pitch and mounting mental health concerns (psychosis-linked homicides, regional system failures, a 100,000-person cohort study) signal hospital-flow and mental health funding pressure and evaluation demand. Rebate and fee settings will matter for state and Commonwealth funding negotiations and for ageing-population policy.

synthesis.brief: Education ministers have agreed the biggest school system shake-up in years. It includes proposed national exams for Years 6, 10 and 12, plus a screen and AI 'digital detox' in classrooms. Expect demand for assessment design, curriculum alignment, implementation planning and evaluation, and for guidance on edtech and AI procurement and policy. Early childhood is under separate pressure: a childcare chain has collapsed amid closures, enrolments are falling and the Coalition is shaping an opposition childcare plan. That points to market-stewardship and sustainability work.
